reviewBoundary: Three new complete senior fifteen-gap four-choice narratives. Fictional incidents; no invented study, statistics or past-paper authorship. Same-author key and all-alternative review, with shuffled presentation. No independent teacher or learner calibration claimed.

units.title: A place on the back page
units.alignmentNote: Level/family drafting reference only. Final practice is one complete National I-style fifteen-gap four-choice original passage, with no copied source prose or answer keys.

materials.title: A place on the back page
materials.text:
For the school newspaper, I chose my sharpest sports-day photograph: the winning runner crossing the line with both arms ____1____. It seemed perfect for the front page.

The student editor stopped at another image I had nearly ____2____. It showed two runners behind the track, one helping the other tie a shoe. Their faces were partly hidden.

"What happened here?" she asked.

One runner's lace had broken. A competitor had offered a spare, and both had returned to their places before the ____3____.

The editor asked me to speak to them. Why did we need an ____4____ for a technically imperfect photograph? Still, both agreed to talk. The spare lace came from a bag of old equipment. The act had seemed ____5____ to them; they were surprised somebody had noticed.

I wrote a short account and checked it with them. When the newspaper appeared, the winner was on the front page. My other photograph was on the back, beside the ____6____.

I wished it had been larger. Then a younger student stopped me. Where could her club keep spare equipment so anyone could ____7____ it? The story had given her an idea.

I began to understand why the editor had ____8____ at that image. A photograph could do more than record victory. It could draw attention to something easy to ____9____.

I still work on sharpness and light. Those skills ____10____. But I also look beyond the obvious centre of an event. I ask permission before telling someone's story and ____11____ the details instead of guessing from an image. That back-page picture made me more ____12____ about what I might have missed. It had not replaced the winner's ____13____; it had added another moment to the record.

Next sports day, I took fewer pictures but spent more time ____14____ to the people in them. My work felt more ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Celebrating the finish with both arms raised fits the victory scene. Hidden, folded and covered do not describe that celebratory gesture.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The partly hidden, imperfect shot had nearly been deleted. Selling, framing and borrowing do not describe removing an unwanted digital photograph.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: They return to race positions before the start. Interview and prize are later events, and photograph is already being taken.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Speaking to both runners is an interview to establish the story. No apology, advertisement or argument is the requested reporting task.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The runners had considered the help ordinary and were surprised it drew notice. Expense, impossibility and danger are not features of lending a spare lace.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The written account accompanies the back-page image. Price, schedule and another portrait are not what the narrator wrote.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Shared spare equipment should be available for anyone to use. Hiding, selling and measuring do not serve that accessible club resource.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The editor stopped at this image, so paused. Laughter, wandering and shouting do not describe that close attention.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Quiet preparation behind the track is easy to overlook. Repair, announce and repeat do not mean failing to notice it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Continuing to improve photographic technique shows those skills matter. Vanish or wait do not explain that value; change is not the reason given.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Responsible reporting checks details with the people involved. Inventing, concealing and replacing undermine that accuracy.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Questions about missed events show curiosity. Certainty and carelessness resist enquiry, while anger is not supported.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The additional account does not replace the winner's achievement. Equipment, permission and address are not the success being acknowledged.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The improved reporting spends time listening to subjects. Pointing, returning and waving do not gather their account.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Helping readers notice a useful act gives the work meaning. Cost, privacy and hurry do not express the new value.

units.title: The pods outside the basket
units.alignmentNote: Level/family drafting reference only. Final practice is one complete National I-style fifteen-gap four-choice original passage, with no copied source prose or answer keys.

materials.title: The pods outside the basket
materials.text:
At the end of the gardening season, I helped Grandma photograph our bean ____1____ for the village show. I filled a basket with fresh green pods and moved three dry brown ones off the table, ready to ____2____ them.

"Open one first," Grandma said.

Inside were several hard beans. The pod had looked ____3____ beside the fresh vegetables, but Grandma wanted to keep its ____4____. 

"These are for next spring," she explained.

I had thought the season ended when everything was picked. Grandma showed me paper packets she had ____5____ from earlier years. Each carried the date and a short note about the plants. 

She did not promise that every seed would grow. Soil, weather and care still mattered. Saving them kept a future crop ____6____; it did not guarantee that crop.

We worked slowly, checking that the seeds were dry before packing them. I wanted to finish quickly, but Grandma remained ____7____. 

She asked me to ____8____ the seeds between two packets. We would plant one group and keep the other until we knew whether the first had grown well. Then I wrote a clear ____9____ on each, rather than trusting that I would remember its contents.

The following spring, I helped sow the first packet. Some seeds failed, but several plants developed. Watching them, I thought about the brown pods I had almost put in the ____10____.

They had not looked like a prize-winning part of the harvest. Their value belonged partly to the ____11____. The photograph no longer showed everything important about that season.

Grandma let me keep the second packet. It was a small ____12____ to care for, not a guarantee of success. I understood why she had recorded where the seeds came from: those notes helped the next gardener make a ____13____ choice. At the village show, I put the packets beside the photograph. A harvest could be something to ____14____ and something that helped the story ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The picked beans are the harvest being photographed. Journey and schedule are different events, and the village show is the competition rather than the beans.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The narrator nearly throws them into waste, so discard. Sale, weighing and naming do not match the later almost-binned pods.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Beside fresh vegetables, dry brown pods initially look worthless to the narrator. Price, perfection and colourful appearance are not the dismissed quality.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Hard beans inside the dry pod are kept as seeds for spring. Leaves, roots and flowers are not the contents described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Dated packets from previous years have been saved. Erasing or breaking prevents their use, and the text distinguishes packets she retained from seeds originating with friends.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Saving seed preserves a possible future crop without guaranteeing it. Familiar, finished and private do not express that possibility-versus-certainty distinction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Slow careful checking despite impatience demonstrates Grandma's patience. Anger and silence are not indicated, while carelessness contradicts the checks.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Putting seed into two packets divides it. Counting alone does not distribute it; hiding and selling do not create the two planned groups.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: A written label identifies each packet's contents. Picture, price and map do not express the identifying note contrasted with memory.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The opening intended discard is later recalled as almost putting them in the bin. Basket and show keep them, while planting in ground is their eventual use.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Seeds' value includes a future season. Weather affects it but does not name the time contrast; past and photograph are the already recorded season.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The entrusted packet is a responsibility to care for. It is not an awarded prize, a payment or an argument.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Origin notes inform the next gardener's choice. Speed, popularity and fashion are not the basis of these recorded observations.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The full harvest is something to celebrate while seeds carry it forward. Postponing, forgetting and replacing do not fit the positive village display.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Seeds help the garden's story continue into another season. Stop, disappear and shrink do not express that continuing growth.

units.title: The stone that stayed interesting
units.alignmentNote: Level/family drafting reference only. Final practice is one complete National I-style fifteen-gap four-choice original passage, with no copied source prose or answer keys.

materials.title: The stone that stayed interesting
materials.text:
I found a black stone beside a path outside town. Its shiny surface and strange holes looked ____1____, and I immediately imagined it had fallen from space. I took it to school, hoping our science teacher would share my excitement.

She asked me to ____2____ exactly where I had found it. Then she suggested showing it to a museum specialist rather than announcing my discovery as a fact. I wanted to be ____3____ already, but agreed to wait.

The specialist was kind. After looking closely, he said it was probably waste from metalworking, not a meteorite. I felt ____4____. The story I had prepared for my friends suddenly seemed foolish.

He noticed my expression and invited me to ____5____ the stone with him. Its features were still worth describing. He explained which observations supported his view and which would need further checking.

"Does being from here make it ____6____?" he asked.

I had no answer. He found an old map showing workshops near the path. My note about the location became a useful piece of ____7____. The stone might help tell a local ____8____ story, even if it told no story about space.

Back at school, I changed my presentation. I described the object ____9____, separating what I had observed from what I had first imagined. I made a small ____10____ giving the location and the specialist's explanation, rather than calling it a meteorite.

Some friends still liked my first idea better. I understood why: I had liked it too. But an exciting ____11____ was not a reason to ignore a more likely account.

The stone stayed on my desk. It had not lost my ____12____; it had changed the questions I asked. Instead of asking only whether it came from space, I began with a smaller ____13____: what could its features actually tell me? Waiting for an answer required being ____14____. It also left the world around my own town more ____15____ than I had expected.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The strange shiny object appears unusual and inspires an extraordinary guess. It is visible and no softness or previous familiarity is established.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The exact location must be recorded as evidence. Changing/hiding would damage provenance and guessing would not preserve what was known.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The narrator wants immediate certainty about a space origin. Politeness and quietness are different behaviours; patience is what waiting requires, not what the narrator initially wants to avoid.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A likely local-industrial origin disappoints the expected space discovery. Relief, pride and boredom do not fit the collapsed imagined story.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The specialist invites close examination of its features. Purchase, decoration and concealment do not investigate the object.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: He challenges the idea that local origin makes the stone uninteresting. Distance, absence of weight and price are not the lost-value assumption being questioned.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The recorded location supports a link with nearby workshops, making evidence. It is not apparatus, authorisation or decoration.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Old workshops connect it with local industrial history. Weather, travel and sports are not the map-based account.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Separating observations from guesses makes the description accurate. Anger and secrecy undermine enquiry; brevity is not the distinction described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: An identifying label gives location and explanation. A promise, award or travel ticket does not describe that written display information.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The space origin is an exciting possibility, not an established fact. Accident, instrument and appointment do not name the proposed explanation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The narrator remains interested and changes questions, preserving curiosity. Weight and colour have not been lost, and the owner is still the narrator.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The quoted enquiry is a question. Payment, victory and secrecy do not name the new investigative starting point.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Waiting for a supported answer requires patience. Fame and silence are not required, while quickness contrasts with careful waiting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The local world becomes more interesting through new questions. Ordinary and predictable remove that discovery, while distant contradicts attention to the narrator's own town.
